logic_node.action_detail: In patients with advanced HF, when consistent with patient's goals of care, timely referral for HF specialty care is recommended to review HF management and assess suitability for advanced HF therapies (LVAD, cardiac transplantation, palliative care, palliative inotropes).

source_text: In patients with advanced HF, when consistent with the patient's goals of care, timely referral for HF specialty care is recommended to review HF management and assess suitability for advanced HF therapies (eg, LVAD, cardiac transplantation, palliative care, and palliative inotropes).

logic_node.action: Consider fluid restriction for congestion symptoms
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with advanced HF and hyponatremia, the benefit of fluid restriction to reduce congestive symptoms is uncertain. Evidence is low quality and fluid restriction only improves hyponatremia marginally.

source_text: For patients with advanced HF and hyponatremia, the benefit of fluid restriction to reduce congestive symptoms is uncertain.

logic_node.action: Identify advanced HF by clinical indicators
logic_node.action_detail: Clinical indicators of advanced HF include: repeated hospitalizations or ED visits for HF in the past 12 months, need for IV inotropic therapy, persistent NYHA class III-IV symptoms despite therapy, intolerance to RAASi or beta blockers, need to escalate diuretics (furosemide equivalent >160 mg/d or metolazone), refractory congestion, progressive renal or hepatic dysfunction, worsening right HF or secondary pulmonary hypertension, frequent SBP <=90 mmHg, cardiac cachexia, persistent hyponatremia (sodium <134 mEq/L), refractory ventricular arrhythmias or frequent ICD shocks, and predicted 1-year mortality >20%.

source_text: Clinical Indicators of Advanced HF: Repeated hospitalizations, need for IV inotropic therapy, persistent NYHA III-IV symptoms, intolerance to RAASi/beta blockers, escalating diuretics, refractory congestion, progressive renal/hepatic dysfunction.

logic_node.action: Assess exercise capacity for advanced HF
logic_node.action_detail: Severely reduced exercise capacity indicating advanced HF is defined as: peak VO2 <14 mL/kg/min or <50% predicted, 6-minute walk test distance <300 m, or inability to walk 1 block on level ground because of dyspnea or fatigue.

source_text: Severely reduced exercise capacity (peak VO2, <14 mL/kg/min or <50% predicted, 6-min walk test distance <300 m, or inability to walk 1 block on level ground because of dyspnea or fatigue).

logic_node.action: Classify advanced HF by INTERMACS profile
logic_node.action_detail: INTERMACS profiles stratify advanced HF patients: Profile 1 (critical cardiogenic shock with life-threatening hypotension and escalating inotropic/pressor support), Profile 2 (progressive decline despite inotropic support), Profile 3 (stable but inotrope dependent), Profile 4 (resting symptoms on oral therapy at home), Profile 5 (exertion intolerant, housebound), Profile 6 (exertion limited, comfortable at rest with mild activity), Profile 7 (advanced NYHA class III, clinically stable with reasonable activity level).

source_text: The INTERMACS has developed 7 profiles that further stratify patients with advanced HF. Profile 1: Critical cardiogenic shock. Profile 2: Progressive decline. Profile 3: Stable but inotrope dependent. Profile 4-7: Varying degrees of functional limitation.

logic_node.action: Apply I-NEED-HELP mnemonic for advanced HF referral
logic_node.action_detail: I-NEED-HELP mnemonic for triggering advanced HF referral: I (Intravenous inotropes), N (NYHA class IIIB-IV or persistently elevated natriuretic peptides), E (End-organ dysfunction), E (EF <=35%), D (Defibrillator shocks), H (Hospitalizations >1), E (Edema despite escalating diuretics), L (Low systolic BP <=90, high heart rate), P (Prognostic medication intolerance or down-titration of GDMT).

source_text: I-Need-Help: I, Intravenous inotropes; N, NYHA class IIIB to IV or persistently elevated natriuretic peptides; E, End-organ dysfunction; E, EF <= 35%; D, Defibrillator shocks; H, Hospitalizations >1; E, Edema despite escalating diuretics; L, Low SBP <=90; P, Progressive intolerance of GDMT.

logic_node.action_detail: Recent need to escalate diuretics to maintain volume status, often reaching daily furosemide equivalent dose >160 mg/d or use of supplemental metolazone therapy, is a clinical indicator of advanced HF warranting specialist referral.

source_text: Recent need to escalate diuretics to maintain volume status, often reaching daily furosemide equivalent dose >160 mg/d or use of supplemental metolazone therapy.

logic_node.action: Avoid delaying referral until end-organ dysfunction develops
logic_node.action_detail: After patients develop end-organ dysfunction or cardiogenic shock, they may no longer qualify for advanced therapies (LVAD, cardiac transplantation). Timely referral before clinical deterioration is critical. A complete assessment is not required before referral.

source_text: After patients develop end-organ dysfunction or cardiogenic shock, they may no longer qualify for advanced therapies. A complete assessment of the patient is not required before referral.
